  • The static type of a collection operator keeps the missing element of an operand whose cells can be absent. With L: list<integer | missing>, Join(L, [2]) and ListJoin(L, [2]) were typed list<number>, which excludes the Missing cell of the value; they are now typed list<integer | missing>, as Append(L, 2) already was. The same holds for DeleteAt, Partition, Chunk, ChunkBy, GroupBy, Zip, TakeWhile, DropWhile, RandomShuffle, Dedup, Cycle, ListFrom, SetFrom, DictionaryFrom, Values, Map with a function literal, Find, MaxBy, MinBy, and the set operations (Union(S, {2}) with S: set<integer | missing> is set<integer | missing>, where it was the bare set). A position or a count over such a list is an integer: IndexWhere, ArgMax, ArgMin and CountIf were typed number, and Position list<number>. Flatten of such a list is list<any>, where it was the bare list. An operand typed with any elements is treated the same way, because any admits an absent value: Flatten(M) with M: list<list<any>> and Union(A, {2}) with A: set<any> are list<any> and set<any>, where they were the bare list and set.

  • A sum or product whose operand type has an imaginary member is typed complex, because neither is closed over the imaginary numbers (i + (-i) = 0, i · i = -1). With r: imaginary | integer, r + 1 was typed imaginary | integer, which excludes its value 1 + i; it is now complex. The same holds for an alias of such a union, for list and tuple cells ([i] + [-i] is vector<complex^1>, where it was vector<imaginary^1> with the value [0]), for a list of points plus a point, and for imaginary | nan, which becomes complex | nan. A sum of two lists of ranges, [1..3] + [1..3], is typed list<list<integer>^1>, where it was list<range^1>.

  • Arithmetic over a list whose element can be a list or absent has a static type that holds the result. With L: list<list<integer> | missing> and L := [[1, 2], Missing], L + 1 was typed list<list<number>>, but the absent element becomes NaN; it is now typed list<list<number> | nan>. A function over a list of rows and numbers keeps the rows: Sin(L) with L: list<list<integer> | integer> was typed list<number> and is now list<list<number> | number>. An absent row of points stays Missing, also when the point type is the bare tuple (it was NaN).

  • Collection operators whose result can hold Missing say so in their type. Iterate(f, Missing) and an Iterate whose callback can return Missing are typed list<any>, where they were the values-only list. First([]), Last([]) and At([], 2) are typed missing, where they were unknown. Map with a callback that is declared for numbers or booleans over a source whose elements can be collections (Map(Sqrt, U) with U: any) admits a collection element; with a callback such as IsPrime or Not over a list that can hold Missing, the element type has a missing arm. Map with a user function that has no declared result types the call: with g := c ↦ If(c == "a", "zz", c), Map(g, ["a", "b"]) was typed as the source and is now typed by what g returns. A Zip element whose items are all absent is Missing through .at() and iteration too, as it already was in the printed value, and compiled JavaScript writes it as an absent value; the Python target declines such a Zip.

  • A complex number whose imaginary coefficient is written as an inline fraction keeps its value in a LaTeX round trip. At a deep level, or with an inline fractionStyle, Complex(1/10, 1/10) was written 1/10+1/10\imaginaryI, which reads back as 1/10 + 1/(10i), the opposite imaginary part. It is written 1/10+(1/10)\imaginaryI (found by Tycho's round-trip audit of its Desmos corpus, whose failing trees are now part of npm run check:roundtrip).

  • A mixed number keeps its tree in a LaTeX round trip (Tycho ledger row 390). 2\frac{1}{2} is the sum Add(2, 1/2), which was written 2+\frac{1}{2} with prettify: false and read back as 5/2. It is written as the mixed number whenever the parser rebuilds the same sum from it, with or without prettify: -2\frac{1}{2} was written -\frac{1}{2}-2, and 500\frac{999}{1000} was written 500+\frac{999}{1000}. The pretty MathJSON of -3\frac{1}{4} is ["Add", -3, ["Rational", -1, 4]] (it was ["Subtract", ["Rational", -1, 4], 3]). The fraction of a mixed number is always written \frac{…}{…}: with an inline fraction style, -2\frac{1}{2} was written -21/2. A fraction that is an integer is not a mixed number: 2\frac{4}{2} is 4 (it was the sum Add(2, 2)), and Add(2, Rational(3, 1)) is no longer written 2\frac{3}{1}, which read back as 6.

  • Printing an unevaluated lazy view does not run a side effect. toString(), the latex getter and toLatex() evaluated the cells of a view over a list literal to show a preview: printing Dedup([1, H(1), 2]), with H declared pure: false, called H twice, a view over Random() printed a different list each time, and a comprehension whose body assigns an outside variable did the assignment. Such a view now prints as written (Reverse([1, H(1), 2])), and its value comes from .evaluate(). A view over pure functions, or one that writes only to its own local variables, still shows its preview. The same holds when the view calls a comprehension index or a callback parameter whose functions can be impure: [q(1) for q in [a ↦ H(a)]] and Map(w ↦ w(1), fs), with fs holding such functions, print as written.

  • In Epsil, a function statement in a function body works when its name is also the name of a library constant. function o() { function i() { 2 }; i() } then o() gave Error(ErrorCode("constant-assignment", "i")) instead of 2; the same happened for e, Pi and the other library constants. The definition was written to the library constant instead of making a binding local to the call. It is now local to each call of the outer function, as at the top level, and the library constant outside the body does not change.

  • Two quantities whose units have the same dimension compare by their physical value on every route. isEqual(), isIdenticallyEqual(), is(), isLess(), isLessEqual(), isGreater() and isGreaterEqual() gave undefined or false for 1000 m and 1 km, because the unit symbols counted as unknowns; now they agree with Equal. NotEqual is the negation of Equal (1000 m ≠ 1 km is False, 6 W ≠ 7 W is True; both stayed unevaluated). Max, Min, Clamp and Sort order such quantities with no tolerance: Max(1 km, 999 m) and Max([1 km, 999 m]) are 1 km (they stayed unevaluated). The comparison converts both quantities to the finer of the two units, so 1 eV = 2 eV is False (it was True, because the difference in joules was smaller than the tolerance). It applies temperature offsets: 0 °C = 273.15 K is True and 0 °C < 1 K is False (they were False and True). Two exact magnitudes are compared with exact arithmetic, also when they are too large for a double (10^400 m < 10^401 m) or when their double cancels: 1 m = (1 + 10^-16) m is False. Under .N(), the exact magnitude of a quantity decides, as it does for a number: 1 m < (1 + 10^-30) m is True. The conversion is exact between two identical units and for every unit defined by an exact decimal number (in, ft, mi, lb, eV and all SI prefixes); the angle units and Da are compared within the tolerance. A magnitude with no numeric value or a complex value, even with a very small imaginary part, leaves the comparison unevaluated: x m = y m was True and x m < y m was False. Quantities of different dimensions, and a quantity and a plain number, stay unevaluated.

  • Sort and Ordering of a lazy source give the error of an element that fails: with h(2) an error, Sort(Map(h, [2])) was [Error(…)] and Sort(Map(h, [3, 2, 1])) stayed unevaluated. Each element of the source is read once. A membership test (Element, NotElement, Contains) over a lazy source that computes a failed element gives that element's error when it finds no match: 5 ∈ Map(h, [1, 2]) was False. A Range or an Interval keeps its arithmetic test, and an infinite source is not walked.

  • Count(xs, p) gives the error when the predicate fails on an element, as CountIf does. Before, it counted that element as selected: with h(2) failing, Count([1, 2, 3], (u) => h(u) > 0) was 3.

  • On interval-js, a Which or an If arm is also narrowed by a decimal bound written in LaTeX (x \ge 0.5) and by an exact bound that a double holds (\frac{1}{2}) (Tycho ledger row 397). Over [0.49, 0.51], \begin{cases}0 & x\ge0.5\\ \arccos(2x) & \text{otherwise}\end{cases} was partial (domain clipped) and is an interval. A bound that no double holds (\frac{1}{3}) is compiled to an enclosure of its value and still does not narrow.

  • #454 A Fold whose step reads its accumulator by index, such as q(s[1]) with q: (integer) -> list<integer>, is typed from its seed again. The index read had typed the accumulator as a tuple of one integer, and the fold as broadcastable<tuple<integer>>, so compiling the fold at a list<integer> parameter, or compiling acc + fold[1], threw. The fold with seed [1, 0, 1] from the issue is now typed list<integer | nan^3> | vector<integer^2>.

  • An If or Which whose condition may be a list of booleans or a single boolean keeps, in its type, each branch whose element type is not known. With u: list, If(u[2] != 0, p, u) was typed broadcastable<tuple<integer>> for p: tuple<integer>, but returns u itself when the condition is a single False.

  • A seeded Fold or Reduce over a collection that can be empty includes the type of the seed in its type: Fold((a, k) => "x", 0, Range(1, n, 1)) was typed string, but is 0 for n = 0.

  • Assumptions in nested scopes combine: with assume(b ≥ 0) and, in a nested scope, assume(b > 0), b.isPositive and b.isGreater(0) are true (they were undefined), whatever the order of the two facts. With p: integer<1..> and assume(p ≥ 0), p.isPositive is true.

  • On the asynchronous route, a user function whose argument contains a free symbol awaits its body: with f := x ↦ AsyncOnly(x), where AsyncOnly has only an evaluateAsync handler, f(1 {0<t}) gives the value of AsyncOnly(1 {0<t}) (it gave AsyncOnly(1) {0 < t}). The application memo, a list-producing recursion and a numeric evaluation no longer give the synchronous answer for a body that applies such an operator. A recursion over a free symbol still stays inert.

  • After a quantity with the unit newton (\mathrm{N/A^{2}}) is parsed, the operator N still evaluates, and (2 m)^n is written (2\,\mathrm{m})^{n}, so it parses back as the same expression.

  • A list of rows of points whose components have different types ([[(1, 1/2), (1/2, 1)], [(1, 4/3), (3/4, 1)]]) is typed as a 2×2 matrix of points (it was typed as a list of points), and a matrix of points plus a point is typed as a matrix of points (its type held an extra | tuple<…>). A point divided by a vector or matrix with a cell that can be zero has a type that admits the division by zero: (1, 2) / [1, 0] is [(1, 2), (~oo, ~oo)], typed list<tuple<infinity, infinity> | tuple<rational, rational>>. The product of a point and a tensor of rank 3 evaluates, as their quotient does, and a product of a list of points, a matrix and scalar factors is typed as a matrix of points.

  • A Union with more than 100 elements counts and lists a repeated element of a list operand once (Union(L, S).count gave 297 for 150 distinct values).

  • Epsil: an error in the branch of an else if, or in any call whose operator occurs more than once in the statement, is underlined on the branch or argument that holds it (it was the whole statement). When the source does not show which operand of a sum or product holds the error, the whole sum or product is underlined, never an operand that cannot cause it. epsil check reports a function statement for a name that an earlier const bound, with the code invalid-clause-definition, and the run does not report it a second time.

  • With the Rubi rules loaded (loadIntegrationRules), a definite integral of an integrand that is real on the interval no longer gives a complex value: ∫₁²⁰¹¹ √x/(√(2012−x)+√x) dx is 1005 (it was 1005 − 503 ln(−1005) + 503 ln(1005), which is 1005 − 1580.2i). When the integrand is proven real on a finite interval and the difference of the values of the antiderivative at the bounds has an imaginary part, that value is refused: the built-in antiderivative or an exact reduction gives the value, and otherwise the integral stays unevaluated. A correct complex value is kept: ∫₋₁³ √x dx is 2√3 + (2/3)i.

  • simplify() reduces more exact constants:

    • A sum of logarithms of positive rationals or surds with rational coefficients: −2 ln 2 − 2 ln(3/2) + 2 ln 3 is 0 (it stayed as it was), and ln 2 + (1/2) ln 3 is (1/2) ln 12.
    • A quotient whose denominator is a power or a product of a + b√c: (12 − 7√3)/(3 − 2√3)² is −√3/3, and −π(12 − 7√3)/(3 − 2√3)² is (√3/3)·π. So the value of ∫₀^π 1/(2 + cos x) dx simplifies to π√3/3.
    • An odd or even function of a negative constant that is not one number: arctan(−3 + 2√2) is −arctan(3 − 2√2), so arctan(−3 + 2√2) + arctan(3 − 2√2) is 0.

  • With the Rubi rules loaded, a definite integral whose Rubi value is real but written with terms that are not real gets the form of the built-in antiderivative: ∫₂^∞ 1/(x² − 1) dx is ln(3)/2 (it was iπ/2 + artanh(2)).

Performance​

  • On the javascript target, a seeded random draw that reads no input of the compiled function, such as WithRandomSeed(191268, RandomChoice([0, 1], 6561)), is computed once per compiled function, on its first call, and the stored value is read after that: the draw is a pure function of its seed. It was drawn again at every call, about 6,561 numbers per sample of a surface indexed by 9θ + 8φ (0.027 ms per call against 0.0002 ms for sin(9θ + 8φ); now 0.0003 ms). A draw whose seed or body reads an input, a loop index or a caller function, and an unseeded draw, are still per call.

  • A type string that names a type declared with ce.declareType, such as the signature (integer_partition) -> number, is parsed once and then read from a cache. Before, it was parsed twice at every ce.declare. Declaring 1000 functions with such a signature takes about 10 ms, where it took about 47 ms (#453).

  • Equal of two sets, the duplicate removal of Union, and membership in a literal set or list of 32 or more elements group the elements by hash: with 20,000 elements, set equality takes about 4 ms (it took 1.6 s), and the count of a Union of two sets about 50 ms (it took about 3 minutes).

  • A list in which every cell failed is data: it evaluates to itself and is not walked again at each use. In Epsil, 3200 turns of fs = [...fs, g("a")] with a failing g("a") take about 3 s (they took about 20 s).

New Features​

  • FindFit takes an optional fifth argument, a dictionary of options. The global option, FindFit(data, model, params, vars, {global: {b: [0.1, 6]}}), searches the named parameters (at most two) over the given range for the lowest sum of squared residuals, instead of returning the local minimum nearest the start. In the MathJSON dict spelling the range is a two-element array. When the model is linear in every other parameter, the range is scanned on a grid, the other parameters are solved by linear least squares at each grid point, and the lowest grid minima are refined by the bounded Levenberg–Marquardt solver; otherwise the solver runs from each point of a coarser grid and the lowest residual wins. The searched parameter stays inside the range; a range is intersected with the parameter's own (a, a0, lo, hi) bounds. The result record is unchanged; its iterations is the total over every solver run, and a deadline that expires during the search returns the best point found with timedOut: True. An unknown option key, a name that is not a parameter, or a range that is not two finite numbers with lo < hi is an unexpected-argument error. Example: on the five points (1, 4.3), (3.22, 1.18), (5.27, 0.01), (10.49, 1.48), (7.12, 3.44) with the model a\cos(bx+c)+dx+e, the fit from the default start has period 8.0 and a sum of squared residuals of 0.36; with b searched over (0.1, 6) it has period 2.9 and 0.0057.
  • Integrate gives exact values for more families of definite integrals: substitutions that it composes with the existing solver, Beta and Beta-prime forms with logarithmic moments, rational functions of trigonometric and hyperbolic functions, products of Floor, Ceil and FractionalPart with polynomials, polynomially weighted series and telescoping products, and reciprocal pairs of high-degree rational functions. For example, ∫₀¹ x(1−x)^99 dx is 1/10100, ∫₁²⁰¹¹ √x/(√(2012−x)+√x) dx is 1005, and ∫_{1/5}^{5} (1+x²)/(x²+x⁹) dx is 24/5. Most of these reductions run only when the existing routes give no exact value; the splitting at discontinuities, the high-degree reciprocal pairs and the Beta forms with a large power run first, because the existing routes would expand them. Each reduction proves its domain and convergence conditions before it returns a value. The Rubi rules also gain three substitution utilities (SubstForFractionalPowerOfLinear, InverseFunctionOfLinear, SubstForInverseFunction) (#445, contributed by KingArth0r).

0.157.0 2026-10-19​

New Features​

  • NSolve(eq, x) accepts the same arguments as Solve and returns numeric approximations of the solutions.
  • Sum, Product and Table accept the shorthand iterator {i, n}, from 1 to n: Sum(k^2, {k, 3}) is 14. LaTeX tuple iterators such as \mathrm{Integrate}(x, (x,0,1)) also parse correctly.
  • More number theory and combinatorics functions operate element by element on lists: NthPrime([1, 2, 3]) is [2, 3, 5], and Divisors([6, 8]) is [[1, 2, 3, 6], [1, 2, 4, 8]]. Boole, Degrees and DMS also accept lists.
  • Collections can provide three optional handlers, countOf, indexOf and atBigint. Permutations and Combinations use them to answer Element, At, IndexOf and Count without enumerating their elements.

Behavior Changes​

  • Sets are unordered. Equivalent sets now have the same canonical order and compare equal with isSame: {2, 1} prints as {1, 2}, and ListFrom({2, 1}) is [1, 2]. Set patterns match in any order. Set builders, ellipsis notation, and structural or raw sets retain their written order; effects in a canonical set run in canonical order.
  • Operations that depend on position, including Take, Reverse, Sort, Insert, Find, Partition and Scan, consistently reject sets. Convert a set to a list before using these operations.
  • Solve returns families for periodic equations: Solve(sin(x) = 1/2, x) gives [2πt + π/6, 2πt + 5π/6], with integer t. Substitute integers for t or supply a bounded domain to obtain individual values. expr.solve() still returns principal solutions. Cases whose full families cannot be represented remain unevaluated, including unsupported complex families and families requiring additional restrictions.
  • Factorial2 supports negative integers: (−1)!! = 1, (−3)!! = −1, and (−5)!! = 1/3. Negative even integers give ~oo instead of NaN.
  • Quantity arithmetic preserves exact magnitudes: Quantity(3, m)·π is 3π m, and 3 m / 2 m is 3/2. Use .N() for approximations. Conversions by integer factors preserve exactness; other conversion factors give floats.
  • Integer functions preserve float inputs in their results: Fibonacci(5.0) is 5.0, and Divisors(12.0) contains floats. Non-integer inputs remain errors where integers are required.
  • Values supplied as complex.js objects are inexact. For an exact Gaussian integer, use ce.number({ re: 2, im: 3 }) or ce.box(["Complex", 2, 3]).
  • Global declarations cannot replace library constants such as Pi or True. Parameters and local scopes can still use these names. Sequence definitions also cannot replace constants.
  • Float serialization preserves float values through LaTeX and MathJSON round trips. Repeating decimal marks are automatic only for exact values in LaTeX; toMathJson() now defaults repeatingDecimal to false.
  • SVD and SingularValues generally leave exact matrices symbolic under evaluate(); use .N() for numeric decompositions. Small matrices with supported exact singular values retain those results.
  • Rounding functions accept poles: Floor(~oo) is ~oo. Complex numbers with an infinite real part and finite imaginary part become signed real infinity. Sum([1+i, +oo]) and Mean([1+i, +oo]) both give +oo.
  • Epsil reports errors in nested statements, once per source location. Block locals belong to each execution; reading or writing a let or const before its declaration reports read-before-declaration.
  • Products and quotients of square roots stay exact when the combined radicand is above 10⁶: \sqrt{1009}\sqrt{1013} is √1009·√1013 instead of the float 1010.998…, and √1009/√1013 is no longer evaluated to 0.998…. Use .N() for a float. (√−13)^3 evaluates to −13√13·i.
  • An element-wise Which or else-less If with a point branch gives Missing at a position that no clause selects: Which([1, 5] < 3, (1, 2)) is [(1, 2), Missing] instead of [(1, 2), NaN]. A number branch still gives NaN.
  • D(x ↦ a+b, x) canonicalizes to D(a+b, x), so a LaTeX round trip keeps the same tree. A function literal whose body is a single symbol is kept (Tycho row 391).
  • After f(x) is parsed, fy and 2f report the same incompatible-type error as f\times y and 2\times f; they were products. An application such as 2f(x) does not change.
  • IsSquare, IsTriangular, IsOctahedral, IsCenteredSquare, IsHappy and IsAbundant of a symbol stay unevaluated; they answered False.
  • An ordering comparison of a set and a list, such as Less(Set(5, 6), [1, 2]), is an incompatible-type error; it was compared element by element.
  • Join or Append of a dictionary and an element that can never be a key-value entry is an incompatible-type error when boxed: Join(Dictionary(x: 1), [2, 3]) stayed an unevaluated Join.
  • After ce.declare() gives a function a signature, an Epsil function statement for that name replaces the body and keeps the declared signature; it added a clause. A statement with parameters outside the declaration reports invalid-clause-definition.
  • cantorEnumerateComplexNumbers() yields pairs of fractions [[n, d], [n, d]]. The exported factorial2() gives the recurrence value for an odd negative integer.

Issues Resolved​

  • Numeric evaluation of user functions, blocks and lazy Map now agrees with direct evaluation, including exact arguments near a rounding boundary: Map(Sin, [Pi]).N() is [0], and Map(Floor, [(25! − 1)/24!]).N() is [24].
  • Improved rounding of elementary and special functions at high precision, including exact rational arguments, complex angles and incomplete gamma and beta functions. Very small probability tails retain their significant digits (#450, contributed by enumeratio).
  • Solve handles integer-valued float exponents, rejects extraneous roots more reliably, and finds numeric polynomial roots up to degree 1000 within its complexity limits. x^{2.0} = 4 gives 2.0 and -2.0; real-domain pure powers avoid computing complex roots.
  • Improved Series, Limit and Residue at algebraic and symbolic points, including 1 + √2 and π/2. One-sided limits retain their direction; parameter-dependent discontinuities and unsupported branch cuts remain symbolic. For example, lim_{x→a⁺} 1/(x−a) is +∞.
  • Derivatives of blocks with pure local assignments now evaluate: D(Block(k ≔ 2; kx²), x) is 4x.
  • Lazy collections with unknown lengths support more positional reads and reductions: Last(FlatMap([1, 2, 3], x ↦ [x, x])) is 3. Incomplete collections remain symbolic rather than returning partial results, and operations requiring all elements respect maxCollectionSize.
  • Filtering and deduplication use evaluated elements: with x := 5, Dedup([x, 5]) is [5]. Sorting rejects comparators that cannot accept every element. Operations on restricted collections preserve their conditions.
  • Tabulate with a non-positive dimension and ascending Table ranges with no elements return []: Table(k², {k, 2, 0}) is []. Use an explicit negative step to count down.
  • Large Permutations, Combinations and PowerSet no longer overflow the stack or stop early. Permutations and combinations support direct indexing, membership and position queries without enumerating every element.
  • Quantity LaTeX round trips preserve symbolic magnitudes, fractional unit powers, compound units and non-ASCII names such as µm, Å and Ω. Exact magnitudes use siunitx, for example \qty[parse-numbers=false]{2\sqrt{2}}{m}; unsupported unit notation uses Quantity(...). Temperature conversion gives 20 °C = 68 °F accurately.
  • LaTeX round trips preserve derivatives, range steps, blocks, products after sums or limits, and If without an else branch. Small negative numbers and unit exponents print correctly, including with prettify: false (Tycho rows 387–390 and 393–395).
  • Corrected result types for nested list broadcasting, absent points, logical operations, float arithmetic, poles and zero-length collections. Invalid point products and divisions consistently report errors.
  • Compiled assignments preserve caller inputs and the caller's vars object. Python and shader targets handle more blocks, chained assignments and conditionals; unsupported forms decline compilation instead of producing invalid code. Python also handles Unicode name collisions and real sum bounds.
  • Python supports Sum and Product bodies containing statements in supported statement positions. WGSL supports assignment branches used as statements.
  • Compiled functions validate argument counts and preserve absent values during interpreter fallback. Interval results consistently use { kind: 'interval', value: { lo, hi } } or { kind: 'empty' }; conditionals report partial when some inputs have no value and respect branch domains (Tycho row 392).
  • Shader trigonometry is more accurate with large constant offsets. Supported GLSL sine hashes have improved accuracy within the reported float32Bounds; inputs outside those bounds give NaN. Other sensitive Mod/Fract expressions report float32-unsafe-argument warnings. compileFunction() and compileShader() return code without this metadata (Tycho rows 382 and 384).
  • Asynchronous evaluation preserves conditions, awaits operators with only async handlers, and isolates concurrent call and block state. Function redefinitions update dependent expressions consistently.
  • Epsil handles recursive callbacks, standalone do scopes and lists containing errors without host exceptions. Unbounded recursion reports the engine's recursion limit consistently.
  • Operator extensions correctly apply changes to associativity, commutativity and effects. Removing commutativity preserves canonical operand order.
  • Compiled Floor, Ceil, Round, Truncate, Fract, Mod, Sign, Heaviside and comparisons of an exact constant give the interpreter's value, also with constantFold: false: Floor((25! − 1)/24!) compiled to 25 and now gives 24. A rounding function of an integer variable that cannot be rewritten, such as Floor(k·π), declines compilation.
  • An assignment used as an operand compiles correctly: (t ≔ 1) + 2 compiled to t = 1 + 2, which assigned 3. JavaScript and GLSL write (t = 1) + 2; Python and WGSL decline.
  • Sums and products with more than about 120,000 operands no longer throw, NotGreater evaluates, Map accepts Subtract, Negate, Multiply and Divide over points, and -3\,\mathrm{m} parses as the quantity −3 m.

Performance​

  • Faster construction of large sets, matching of large sums, and compilation of expressions with shared subexpressions.
  • Faster numeric evaluation of lazy maps and long sums, with repeated work reused in compiled functions. A 6,000-term numeric sum inside a mapped Sin takes about 60 ms instead of 5.6 s.
  • Faster high precision incomplete gamma and beta evaluation; for example, Gamma(10⁴, 10001) at 524 digits takes about 36 ms instead of 4 s.

0.156.0 2026-10-17​

Issues Resolved​

  • User functions preserve exact arguments for rounding and comparisons under .N(): a function applying Floor to (25! − 1)/24! returns 24.
  • Lazy Map and Filter evaluate impure list elements correctly. Numeric rounding functions also preserve exact surviving elements when a list drops an element that evaluates to Nothing.
  • Range membership and integer-grid Linspace samples remain exact beyond the safe integer range.
  • Inverse trigonometric functions near complex branch points and HurwitzZeta with severe cancellation remain symbolic when machine precision cannot produce a reliable answer.
  • Corrected types for arithmetic on unions of numbers, points and lists, coordinate accessors, and parameters inferred from index reads.
  • Float half powers retain their float spelling in text output: 2^0.5 prints as 2^(0.5).
  • Declarations inside blocks correctly update dependent expressions.

Performance​

  • Faster repeated evaluation of symbolic function results and lazy broadcasts.

0.155.0 2026-10-17​

New Features​

  • ce.undeclare(name) removes a value or function binding from the current scope, including functions defined by multiple clauses.
  • ce.tolerance = "auto" makes tolerance follow the working precision. An explicitly numeric tolerance now survives precision changes (#449).
  • A new broadcast exemption, 'surplus-operands', makes a call with extra operands one error before any broadcast. Numerator, Denominator and NumeratorDenominator use it: Denominator(5, []) is an error, not [].

Behavior Changes​

  • Numeric element-wise operations on symbols typed any or value retain types that allow point and collection results.
  • Compiled predicates must return booleans. Invalid predicates fail compilation or report an error at run time instead of using truthiness.
  • Compiled numeric parameters receive a NaN default for absent arguments; this can change the returned JavaScript function's length property.
  • Unit names such as m, s and K are no longer declared in the system scope, and a Quantity no longer declares its unit names. A function defined in a parent scope does not see a value that a host assigns to one of these names in a child scope unless the parent scope declares the name first, for example with ce.declare('s', 'number').
  • Sum(a) and a = [1, 2] stay unevaluated until a has a value when a is declared any. Operator extensions can change associativity and effects. The type setter refuses a function signature on a constant.

Issues Resolved​

  • Functions inferred from index reads accept list arguments again, including p ↦ p[1] + p[2] (#448). Improved tuple, point, type-alias and overload handling throughout calls.
  • Async user functions, including multi-clause and recursive functions, await their bodies and preserve arguments across overlapping calls. Materializing async maps evaluates their elements asynchronously.
  • Lazy views evaluate their sources once; folds that build lazy accumulators no longer become exponentially slower (#444).
  • Quantity arithmetic preserves symbols and exact roots: 3 m · x is Quantity(3x, m), and sqrt(2 m²) is √2 m. Repeated unit factors combine into powers.
  • Corrected float division, powers and result types. Sqrt(-13)/3 gives (√13/3)i instead of NaN, and DivisorSigma(1, -12) is 28 (#446, contributed by enumeratio; #449).
  • Improved incomplete gamma accuracy for negative non-integer orders and small positive arguments. Numeric integration handles slowly converging endpoint singularities more accurately and detects poles in exponential denominators.
  • Invalid If arity is reported correctly. Derivatives of unsupported blocks and lazy operators stay symbolic without executing their bodies.
  • Sequence definitions respect scopes and constants; removed sequences no longer appear in isSequence() or listSequences().
  • Named and field calls follow redefinitions, parameter names and current bindings. Epsil static checks agree with these rules.
  • Shader sums and products support complex bodies. JavaScript complex mode handles real powers with complex results, and compiled sum indices no longer collide with block locals.
  • Python compiles blocks ending in assignments correctly and rejects reserved names. Reusing a compilation target respects current variable mappings.
  • Point division by a list works in the interpreter and compiled JavaScript: (1, 2)/[1, 2] is [(1, 2), (1/2, 1)].
  • Collection errors include their source trace without reporting failed operands twice. Numerator and denominator operations report extra arguments (#442, contributed by enumeratio).
  • Compiled JavaScript Gamma(x, y) computed Γ(x); it now computes the upper incomplete gamma. The interval target declines the two-argument form (#446, contributed by enumeratio).
  • At over a collection of infinite count whose handler declines a position stays unevaluated instead of giving NaN (#449).
  • LaTeX derivatives with a symbolic order parse as D(f, {x, n}): \partial_x^{n} f was read as a first derivative. \partial_x takes the expression that follows it: \partial_x f + g is D(f + g, x).

Performance​

  • Faster repeated evaluation of symbolic values and nested user functions.

0.154.0 2026-10-15​

New Features​

  • LatexSyntax.dictionary returns the entries of an instance.

Behavior Changes​

  • A tuple with only absent coordinates evaluates to Missing.
  • Functions that consume whole collections keep list arguments whole even through arithmetic or local aliases: with h(xs) := mean(xs^2), h([1, 2, 3]) is 14/3.
  • Measurements propagate uncertainty through more numeric functions and statistics. Sorting, extrema and clamping compare their nominal values.
  • Matrix operations preserve float results when any entry is a float. Exact integer powers are matrix powers; float powers are element-wise: [[1,2],[3,4]]^2.0 is [[1,4],[9,16]] with float entries.
  • Float exponents retain their inexact meaning in simplification and polynomial operations; 0 / 2.5 is 0.0.
  • Function results are checked against their declared result types.
  • Append and Join over a source whose type does not fix its kind are typed collection<T>, not list: with a declared any, Append(a, 1) is typed collection<any>.
  • Comparisons with a Measurement use its nominal value: Less(Measurement(0.7468, 0.001), 1) is True. Floor, Ceil, Round, Truncate and Mod of a measurement return the bare result for its nominal: Floor(Measurement(0.7468, 0.001)) is 0.
  • ce.declare() throws The symbol "Sq" is already declared in this scope when Sq is an operator declared earlier without a signature (the second declaration replaced the first). To change an existing definition, use ce.declare(name, patch, { extend: true }).
  • The add and mul rational helpers exported by @cortex-js/compute-engine/numerics return [±Infinity, 1] for an infinite operand times a finite non-zero one (they returned [NaN, 1]). pow of an infinite base follows IEEE 754 (it threw a RangeError).
  • In Epsil, a bare name -> value call argument is a rule in every position: f(GridLines -> [10, 10]) round-trips. map(x -> x^2, xs) reports mapsto-arrow-expected, with a fixit that replaces -> by => (#435).

Issues Resolved​

  • Definite integrals preserve convergence conditions, detect interior and endpoint divergences more reliably, and evaluate more absolute-value and piecewise integrands exactly: ∫₀^{2π} |sin x| dx is 4 (contributed by KingArth0r).
  • Symbolic integration respects angular units: in degree mode, ∫₀^{180} sin x dx is 360/π.
  • Numeric integration handles near-divergent but convergent powers correctly; ∫₀¹ x^{-0.9999} dx is 10000. Limits compare exponential and algebraic growth correctly: lim_{t→∞} t/e^{√t} is 0.
  • Complex special functions select the correct branch, including LerchPhi(0, 1/3, -8). Argument supports the requested numeric precision, and compiled Gamma handles complex arguments (#428, #439, contributed by enumeratio).
  • Matrix powers follow later assignments of matrix values, preserve matrix shapes, and reject non-square matrices. Empty axes remain in shape types: [[], []] has a 2×0 matrix type.
  • Function calls and named arguments follow redefinitions and updated parameter names. Indexed parameters infer each coordinate separately, and async sums preserve the index captured by callbacks.
  • Lazy collection operations evaluate computed sources correctly. Nested maps and folds preserve accumulator values (#438).
  • Epsil reports errors inside pipe stages, with diagnostics on the relevant argument. Serialized rules preserve library names.
  • Custom LaTeX notation applies inside rewrite rules. Delimiter groups and sequences round-trip correctly, and logarithms stop before an integral's differential. Kronecker delta indices accept spacing and commas.
  • Shader loops follow positive and negative range steps. Compiled calls check parameter types, and compilation metadata describes the emitted numeric mode.
  • Numeric infinities, sequence validation and operator redeclarations report consistent results and errors. Simplifying an unbounded recursive call keeps it symbolic.
  • Compiled HurwitzZeta, LerchPhi, PolyLog, EllipticK, the complete EllipticE, Hypergeometric2F1 and LambertW return complex values in auto and complex mode, where they returned NaN: compiled LerchPhi(3, 2, 1) is 0.7734 - 1.1505i. The GLSL and WGSL targets decline a provably complex value (#434, contributed by enumeratio).
  • Transpose of an operand with no known shape is typed unknown, so MatrixMultiply(q, Transpose(q)) with a free q stays unevaluated instead of returning an incompatible-type error (#439, contributed by enumeratio).

Performance​

  • Faster arithmetic with complex factors and type queries for very large integer literals (#431, contributed by enumeratio).

0.153.0 2026-10-13​

New Features​

  • A host that replaces the At lowering on the javascript target can read a list through a boolean mask with the runtime helper _SYS.atMask(base, mask). Any other index is read by _SYS.atNoWrap.

Behavior Changes​

  • Compiled JavaScript run() expects inputs in the declared shape and returns results that callers must treat as read-only. Pass plain arrays; convert typed arrays once with Array.from(). Keep entries numeric for real list inputs, and copy returned arrays or complex objects before modifying them.
  • simplify() folds pure constant subexpressions whose evaluation gives a numeric literal, with default rules, custom rules or rules: null. Exact symbolic values such as Ln(2) stay symbolic. Numeric relations simplify to truth values: (3 < 4).simplify() is True (#306).
  • Gamma(n) evaluates exactly for positive integers: Gamma(4) is 6 (#429).
  • Numeric evaluation reaches single-statement user-function bodies directly.
  • code of compiled JavaScript reads a constant list of three or more finite real numbers from a _lit_<n> local defined in preamble. A host that evaluates code without run() must include preamble (or preambleOnce once and preamblePerCall on every call). A compile hook must treat an array operand as read-only.
  • CompilationResult.entryPlan no longer has the per-entry checks (entries). A runtime that loads an older stored plan ignores the field.
  • The .pow() method evaluates the root it builds from two number literals: ce.number(-8).pow(ce.number([1, 3])) is -2, not Root(-8, 3) (#430).

Issues Resolved​

  • Wallis-like products with symbolic bounds evaluate to closed forms: ∏_{k=2}^{n} (1 − 1/k²) is (n+1)/(2n).
  • Roots evaluate in one pass with list exponents or assigned fractional exponents: (-8)^{[1/3, 5]} is [-2, -32768] (#430).
  • Async N(x, p) and numeric accuracy goals yield and honor cancellation (#392).
  • Higher-order maps use the callback passed as an argument under .N(). Functions reading stored random expressions retain independent draws.
  • Calls with list arguments have result types derived from their bodies, including parameters passed through unchanged (Tycho row 373).

Performance​

  • Constant lists and matrices in compiled JavaScript are reused across calls.

0.152.0 2026-10-11​

New Features​

  • An operator definition can set evaluatesOperands: true when its handler evaluates every held operand and reads nothing else of them. Under evaluateAsync, the operands are then awaited in order and the handler runs on the values.

Behavior Changes​

  • Provably divergent series evaluate to signed infinity: Σ_{n=1}^{∞} 1/n is +∞. Comparisons with infinity remain undecided when the other operand is not known to be finite (#326).
  • Reduce(…).N() respects the engine's working precision.
  • An engine constructed with precision: 'machine' keeps the faster double-precision fold for Reduce(…).N().

Issues Resolved​

  • Infinite telescoping sums and Wallis products evaluate and simplify correctly: Σ_{k=1}^{∞} 1/(k(k+1)) is 1, and 2∏_{n=1}^{∞} 4n²/(4n²−1) is π (#323, reported by 314systems).
  • Equivalent spellings of sum and product bodies produce the same closed forms.
  • Empty folds and reductions evaluate their initial value. Numeric reductions evaluate elements such as Ln(2) before combining them (#425, reported by enumeratio).
  • Compiled folds support accumulators indexed by their own elements (#425, reported by enumeratio).
  • Async evaluation yields and honors cancellation inside relations, user functions and more lazy operators (#392, contributed by enumeratio).

0.151.0 2026-10-08​

Behavior Changes​

  • Lists and tuples evaluate finite lazy elements while preserving nesting: [map(x => x + 1, [1, 2])] remains [[2, 3]], including when materialized.
  • Integer operations preserve exact integer arguments under .N(): DigitSum(2^1000).N() is 1366.
  • Mod of exact radicals remains exact: Mod(√2, 1) is √2 − 1.

Issues Resolved​

  • GCD and LCM return exact results for large integers: GCD(2^100, 2^50) is 2^50.
  • Mapping lambdas preserves errors and absent values consistently with named callbacks. Mapping a list of functions applies each function correctly.
  • Substitution reaches dictionary values, and dictionaries containing functions round-trip through LaTeX.
  • Parse diagnostics have correct spans after Unicode scripts. Missing scripts retain their bases; Greek names, spaced subscripts and script ordering parse consistently.
  • Loops with symbolic range bounds compile, and literal bounds give indices ranged types. Functions declared to return real values use real arithmetic.
  • If result types retain unknown branches. Errors caused by incorrectly shaped compiled inputs identify the binding.

Performance​

  • Faster interval evaluation of constant subexpressions inside user functions.

0.150.0 2026-10-08​

New Features​

  • New ce.withEvaluationContext(options, fn), for the synchronous work that an evaluateAsync handler does after an await: ce.withEvaluationContext(options, () => x.canonical).evaluateAsync(options).

Behavior Changes​

  • Solve returns every complex polynomial root when no domain is specified, or when solving over the complex numbers. Supported closed forms remain exact: x³ − 2x + 1 = 0 gives [1, (-1 + √5)/2, (-1 − √5)/2].
  • Compiled integer operations reject values outside the safe integer range instead of returning rounded answers. Compiled collection parameters reject unsupported string inputs.
  • Shader targets reject constant collections with more than 256 elements.
  • List literals with lazy spreads evaluate to ordinary lists.
  • Synchronous work that an evaluateAsync handler does after its first await (ce.box(), ce.parse(), evaluate(), canonicalizing a held operand) sees the global scope, not the index of an enclosing Sum. Run it inside ce.withEvaluationContext(options, fn).
  • DSolve writes a complex characteristic root and its conjugate as real modes: y''' - y = 0 gives c₂·e^(-x/2)·cos(√3x/2) + c₃·e^(-x/2)·sin(√3x/2).
  • In the lenient grammar, √2 √3 and √2 ∞ report ambiguous-radical (Tycho row 367).
  • A shader target declines a constant collection of more than 256 elements with the diagnostic code inline-collection-too-large, whose message names the element count and the limit (Tycho row 368).

Issues Resolved​

  • Concurrent async evaluations keep separate scopes, and async handlers resume in the correct scope. N, arithmetic, Evaluate and ReleaseHold yield and await async-only operations (#392).
  • Recursive functions accept whole collection arguments, lazy arguments retain caller bindings, and callbacks over named functions retain computed elements.
  • Exact Range elements remain distinct beyond 2^53. Append permits forward indexing into an infinite source (#422).
  • Seeded random collections retain their seed inside dictionaries, and spreading a map over a set runs its callback once per element.
  • Improved contour and residue integration with float bounds, affine circle notation, exact complex poles and trigonometric multiple angles. Poles inside infinite integration intervals no longer produce finite answers.
  • Contour integrals respect user functions that shadow library names and detect nearby singularities exactly.
  • Series(Zeta(s), s, 1, n) returns the requested Laurent expansion using Stieltjes constants. EllipticPi supports more complex arguments (#421, #422).
  • Improved types for odd real roots, Zip, Repeat, and collections whose elements may be absent.

Performance​

  • Numeric sums and products scale better with many terms. Constant numeric lists are cheaper to compile for interval evaluation.

0.149.0 2026-10-07​

Breaking Changes​

  • Round(x, step) now rounds to a multiple of step. Round(226, 10) is 230; Round(3.14159, 2) is now 4. To round to two decimal places, use Round(3.14159, 1/100) for exact 157/50, or Round(3.14159, 0.01) for float 3.14. Translate decimal-place arguments from other tools accordingly (#417).
  • Negative Take and Drop counts work from the end. Take([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], -2) is [4, 5], and Drop(..., -2) is [1, 2, 3]. Strings behave similarly: Take("hello", -2) is "lo". Negative counts over infinite or unknown-length sources remain unevaluated (#414, reported by enumeratio).
  • expr.count can return a bigint. Its type is now number | bigint | undefined; large finite counts use bigint, while infinite counts use Infinity. Check the type before arithmetic with a JavaScript number. For example, Count(Range(1, 10^20 + 1)) is exactly 100000000000000000001. Indexing from the end of collections with bigint counts is not yet supported (#416, reported by enumeratio).
  • Public complex types now use complex.js 2.4. Update imports of the Complex class from complex-esm to complex.js.

New Features​

  • ce.roundingTies selects the tie rule for Round: "away-from-zero" (default), "to-even", "toward-zero", "toward-positive-infinity", or "toward-negative-infinity". Compiled functions retain the rule selected at compilation. Remainder keeps its existing tie rule (#417, requested by enumeratio).
  • Floor, Ceil and Truncate accept a step: Floor(226, 10) is 220, Ceil(226, 10) is 230, and Truncate(-226, 10) is -220. Exact steps give exact results; float steps give floats (#417, requested by enumeratio).
  • Definite integration supports more piecewise functions, including If, Which, extrema and rounding functions: ∫₋₁¹ max(x, 0) dx is 1/2, and ∫₀³ floor(x) dx is 3 (#413, contributed by KingArth0r).
  • A count collection handler can return a bigint for any count; expr.count converts a safe integer to a number (#416).

Behavior Changes​

  • Running an Epsil program with executeEpsil or the epsil command removes the engine's default iteration limit, so a loop runs until it ends. The engine then keeps no limit for later evaluations, Epsil or not. To keep a bound, assign ce.iterationLimit before running a program.
  • The branch k of LambertW(z, k) must be an integer: LambertW(-1, -0.1) is an incompatible-type error. The branch can be named: lambertW(-0.1, branch: -1) in Epsil, or ["LambertW", -0.1, ["NamedArgument", "'branch'", -1]] in MathJSON (#418, reported by enumeratio).
  • simplify() combines powers with the same base in a product, as it does in a quotient: x^a·x^b is x^(a+b). evaluate() is unchanged (#415, reported by enumeratio).
  • String operators accept a character wherever they accept a string: ToUpperCase(s[1]) is no longer a type error. A symbol with no declared type used at such a parameter is inferred character | string, not string.
  • When the operand types do not select one signature of an overloaded operator, the result type is the union of the possible results: with s of unknown type, Slice(s, 1, 2) is typed list | string, not list.
  • Effect inference is more precise. A local that nested functions only read needs no scope effect, a function has the effects of its let values (let x = Random() makes it random), and a dictionary has the effects of its values ({"a" -> Random()} is random, not pure).

Issues Resolved​

  • Exact range counts, extrema and statistics no longer depend on rounded bounds. Large range statistics avoid enumeration: Sum(Range(1, 10^20)) can return its exact closed form.
  • Take and Drop clamp very large or infinite counts to a finite source's length. Collection queries stay symbolic when elements cannot be determined.
  • Improved numeric stability for very small or large norms and complex values: Norm([3e-200, 4e-200]) is 5e-200 at machine precision.
  • Float division avoids an extra rounding: 0.3/0.3 is 1. Compiled rounding of large integers and Remainder ties agrees with the interpreter.
  • Exact list sums and differences, irrational integration bounds and determinants retain exact values: [√2, 2] + [1, 1] is [1 + √2, 3]. Matrix power rules no longer combine element-wise and matrix operations (#415).
  • Polynomial operators read assigned values. Type inference narrows unions correctly and no longer mistakes collection parameters for matrices.
  • Improved PolyLog and LerchPhi at large orders and arguments; unsupported cases remain symbolic instead of returning inaccurate values (#412, reported by enumeratio).
  • LaTeX preserves parentheses around primed expressions, recognizes Unicode number-set letters, and accepts spaces before postfix operators. Epsil reports -> used in place of a lambda's => (#420, reported by enumeratio).
  • Lenient parsing reports ambiguous-radical for √2 x (Tycho row 366). \mathbb{Z}^- and \mathbb{R}^- name NegativeIntegers and NegativeNumbers.

0.148.0 2026-10-05​

New Features​

  • N(x, [p, a]) accepts significant-digit and absolute-accuracy goals, stopping when either is met. Use PositiveInfinity to disable one goal: N([π, 1000π], [PositiveInfinity, 3]) is [3.142, 3141.593]. The engine's precision is preserved; results remain symbolic if a goal cannot be met (#391).
  • Compiled JavaScript can run without a Compute Engine instance. Import createJavaScriptRuntime from @cortex-js/compute-engine/runtime and use runtime.load(result) to load a compilation artifact. Runtime versions must match. Functions supplied as source cannot retain enclosing closures (#372, contributed by enumeratio).
  • ResidueClass(k, n) represents modular values: ResidueClass(7, 5) is ResidueClass(2, 5), and 1/ResidueClass(3, 7) is ResidueClass(5, 7). Arithmetic requires compatible moduli and invertible divisors. QuotientRing(Integers, n) now contains residue classes rather than integers (#399, #411, contributed by enumeratio).
  • Contour integration supports circles, rectangles and simple polygons through ce.contourIntegrate(), ContourIntegrate, and LaTeX \oint notation. Reports include poles, residues and the integral. A pole on the contour gives Indeterminate; unsupported cases remain symbolic (#410).
  • More real integrals evaluate exactly using residues: ∫_{−∞}^{∞} sin(x)/x dx is π, and ∫₀^{2π} dx/(2 + cos x) is 2π/√3. Principal values must be requested explicitly with RealLineContour(True).
  • Complex numeric evaluation now covers Bessel and Airy functions, Sinc, Fresnel functions, and every integer branch of LambertW. Error functions and trigonometric integrals also support imaginary-axis arguments.
  • CompilationResult has the new fields runtimeVersion, preambleOnce, preamblePerCall, callCode, entryPlan and reconstructionDigits. createJavaScriptRuntime() accepts the options random, frame, iterationLimit and deadline. With random: null, a draw throws a CapabilityDeniedError; test e.name, not instanceof (#372).

Behavior Changes​

  • Absolute-value bars on a set or string give its size: |{1, 2}| is 2.
  • Solve returns a list only when it can establish completeness. Otherwise it stays unevaluated, and expr.solve() returns null. Unsupported computed collections are type errors rather than empty solution lists.
  • N consistently returns inexact numbers, preserves ce.precision, and rounds collection elements: N([1/3, Pi], 4) is [0.3333, 3.142] (#391, #409).
  • Numeric operations reject set operands rather than pairing them by position. Scalar function parameters broadcast over tuple components: Apply((u: real) ↦ 2u, (a, b)) is (2a, 2b).
  • Calls awaiting a list's value remain symbolic until it is known, preserving future broadcasting. Invalid scalar arguments give consistent type errors.
  • Argument/Arg returns angles in the engine's angular unit.
  • Lenient parsing reads √12 as √(12), multi-digit subscripts as whole subscripts, and sin^{-1}(x) as arcsin(x). It adds ambiguity diagnostics for inputs with another common interpretation.
  • The default time limit for loadIntegrationRules() is now 120 seconds.
  • evaluate() returns a sequence term that is exact but not a number literal: for B_n = π·B_{n−1}/n with B_0 = 1, B_10 is π^10/10!; it stayed unevaluated. ce.getSequenceTerms() returns such terms, and ce.getSequenceCache() holds only exact terms.
  • When the unknown has no declared type and no domain is given, Solve gives all roots of a polynomial, complex roots included (x^2 + 1 = 0 is [i, −i]), and only the real solutions of other equations. A parameter of the equation with no declared type is real.
  • N(Measurement(v, δ), p) keeps the uncertainty and rounds v, so N(Integrate(…), p) is a Measurement.
  • Derivative(f) is a function literal also when its closed form holds the derivative of another function: with h(x) := g(x)·x, Derivative(h) is (x) ↦ x·Apply(Derivative(g, 1), x) + g(x).

Issues Resolved​

  • Dictionaries and strings containing special characters round-trip through LaTeX and MathJSON. Fractions, negative terms, derivatives and compound powers serialize with the grouping needed to preserve their meaning (#345).
  • Lenient parsing preserves digits, Greek names, function subscripts and script order. Epsil accepts f(x) := body as a function definition (#400, contributed by enumeratio).
  • Solve respects bounded domains and angular units, solves more systems and avoids incomplete root lists. Lambert W templates retain only real roots where real solutions are required.
  • Improved real and complex special-function accuracy, including Bessel, Fresnel, error and integral functions. LambertW(-1/e) and LambertW(-1/e, -1) are exactly -1.
  • Limits at infinity respect complex values and unknown coefficient signs; NLimit at −∞ samples negative arguments. Divergent integrals and numeric error estimates are handled more reliably (#396, #405).
  • Lazy collections retain local bindings and update when sequence dependencies change. Unavailable elements no longer make finite collections appear empty.
  • Point norms validate component lengths, handle empty point lists and compile on more targets. Function literals and named calls enforce parameter types consistently.
  • Added symbolic derivatives for Arctan2 and more multi-argument functions; partial derivatives compile and evaluate more efficiently.
  • Simplification preserves list shape, respects user replacements of library functions, and applies angular identities only in radians. Integration also respects user function definitions and avoids unbounded searches.
  • Shader compilation supports function primes, fixed-length maps, vector squares and more applied derivatives.
  • A memoized sequence term is computed again when a symbol that its recurrence reads changes. A first read of a large index no longer overflows the call stack: F_2000 of the Fibonacci recurrence gives its 418 digits.
  • Arcosh(0) and Arcoth(0) evaluate to iπ/2, and EllipticK(0) and EllipticE(0) to π/2. A sum whose radical-coefficient terms cancel is 0: (√2/4·x).sub(√2/4·x) was 0·x (#409).
  • Count of set operations is correct: Count(SymmetricDifference({1, 2, 3}, {2, 3, 4})) is 2; it was 1.
  • With a user value of Pi, evaluate() no longer uses the library π: with Pi equal to 3, sin(π) is sin(3); it was 0.
  • D(f(x), f) stays symbolic; it was 0.
  • A product whose LaTeX ends with a symbol keeps a \times before a parenthesized factor: 2v\times(x+1). The form 2v(x+1) read back as a call of v.
  • Compiled JavaScript calls the current value of a block-local function that is assigned again: let h = (k) => k + 1; h := (k) => k + 2; h(3) gives 5, as in the interpreter. It gave 4.

0.147.0 2026-10-02​

New Features​

  • Added Wolfram Language aliases EulerPhi, PartitionsP and Det.
  • Lenient parsing reports more ambiguous notation, including inverse functions, primes and scripts.

Behavior Changes​

  • Totient and NPartition evaluate at zero and negative integers.
  • Exact non-integer factorials remain symbolic under evaluate(); .N() follows the working precision and supports factorials beyond float64 range.
  • Host complex values with integer parts are exact; computed complex floats retain their inexactness, including very small components.
  • Arctan and Arccot use branch-cut values consistent with odd symmetry: Arctan(-2i) is approximately −π/2 − 0.549i.
  • Lenient parsing gives ** the same precedence as ^: -x**2 is -(x²). Chains containing only ** still associate from the right.
  • An exact complex number divided by an exact number is one exact complex literal: i/3 is ["Complex", 0, ["Rational", 1, 3]], and 2/i is -2i.
  • Numeric routines return floats also when the value is an integer: NIntegrate(1, 0, 2) is 2.0, not 2. This also applies to NLimit, ND, NDSolve, FindFit and FindRoot.
  • The rational eigenvalues of an exact matrix larger than 3×3 are exact, and Eigenvectors then gives exact vectors.

Issues Resolved​

  • Exact multiples of π reduce correctly under .N() and in compiled code. Compiled negative-base powers agree with the interpreter's real-root rules.
  • Improved complex Gamma, Factorial, BarnesG and inverse trigonometric evaluation beyond the double range. Branch cuts, small imaginary parts and high precision complex results are preserved.
  • Compiled JavaScript retains small complex components and consistently represents complex infinity. Compiled StieltjesGamma is accurate through order 30.
  • Numeric functions evaluate random operands once. NaN components propagate correctly through complex results.
  • Lenient parsing handles spaces and duplicate superscripts consistently; primed function names and factorials serialize with correct grouping.

0.146.0 2026-10-02​

New Features​

  • Added modular roots and reconstruction: PowerModList(3, 1/2, 11) is [5, 6], PowerMod(4, 1/2, 7) is 2, and RationalReconstruction(6, 11) is 1/2. Also added PrimitiveRootList and a target-list form of MultiplicativeOrder.
  • Added DirichletEta, DirichletBeta, DirichletCharacter and DirichletL: DirichletEta(1) is ln 2, DirichletBeta(1) is π/4, and DirichletCharacter(5, 2, 2) is i.
  • Added generalized Stieltjes constants: StieltjesGamma(0) is EulerGamma; StieltjesGamma(n, a) supports orders through 30.
  • Added LogGamma, BarnesG and LogBarnesG. LogGamma is the analytic continuation of log gamma, with branch values distinct from GammaLn. BarnesG(5) is exactly 12; PolyGamma(-1, z) is LogGamma(z).
  • Added ClausenCl(n, θ): ClausenCl(2, π/2) is CatalanConstant.
  • Added StirlingS2 as an alias for Stirling.

These additions were contributed by enumeratio (#395).

Behavior Changes​

  • Integrals, sums and products with only one bound remain unevaluated.
  • Divergent definite integrals return signed infinity or Indeterminate when divergence is established. Unresolved pole locations remain symbolic.
  • NIntegrate tries quadrature first, and constant numeric integrals can be folded during compilation.
  • PrimitiveRoot and MultiplicativeOrder ignore the modulus sign.
  • In \sum_{k=1} and \prod_{k=1}, the subscript is the lower bound, not the upper bound.
  • A sum with a lower bound and no upper bound is no longer a sum to infinity under .N(). For an infinite sum, write the upper bound +∞ (\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}).
  • The signature of NIntegrate is (function, lower:number, upper:number) -> number. A Tuple of bounds or a missing bound is an error. For a multiple integral, use Integrate(f, Limits(x, …), Limits(y, …)).N().
  • Compiled Python inverse trigonometric and inverse hyperbolic functions of a complex argument always return a Python complex, also when the value is real.

Issues Resolved​

  • Numeric integration handles endpoint singularities, moving poles, nested divergent integrals and reversed bounds more reliably. Slowly converging integrals have improved values and error estimates.
  • Oscillatory semi-infinite integrals work in interpreted and compiled code: ∫₀^∞ sin x/x dx is π/2 to about 11 decimal places.
  • Definite integration detects poles from assigned values, constants and logarithmic denominators. Flat MathJSON bounds parse consistently for integrals, sums and products.
  • Improved inverse trigonometric and hyperbolic accuracy for large, small and complex arguments. Python and shader targets follow the correct branch cuts.
  • GammaLn is more accurate near 0, 1 and 2. Compiled JavaScript preserves small complex results.
  • FromDigits and ChineseRemainder reject non-integer elements; infinite input collections no longer exhaust memory. Stirling and Eulerian numbers outside their valid triangle return 0.
  • Redefined control operators compile as user definitions. Copies of library operators retain their names and supported derivatives.
  • Missing arguments and invalid logarithm arity report normal expression errors. Restrictions with infinite condition lists no longer run out of memory.
  • ∫ ln(x + 1) dx is (x + 1)·ln(x + 1) − x. It was (x + 1)·ln(x) − x + 1, and ∫₀¹ ln(x + 1) dx was +∞.
  • Compiled Python Arccot of a complex argument with a negative real part is no longer off by π.

0.145.0 2026-10-01​

New Features​

  • Add notation after engine construction with ce.latexSyntax.addEntries(entries) (#393).
  • Load custom libraries with ce.loadLibrary(library), and query a definition's library with ce.libraryOf(name) (#393).
  • Extend an operator with ce.declare(name, patch, { extend: true }). Unspecified fields are retained; addSignature adds an overload (#394).
  • Operator definitions can provide partial derivatives with the derivative key. Evaluation handlers receive a precision option for numeric requests (#393).
  • Lenient parsing reports more ambiguous-* diagnostics for notation such as x^2y, sin x y, 1..10..2 and log(x, 2). Use ce.parse(text, { strict: false, onAmbiguity: 'error' }) to turn ambiguous readings into expression errors; the default is 'report'.
  • The new exponentialE serialization option sets how ExponentialE and Exp are written. The imaginaryUnit option now also sets how ImaginaryUnit and complex numbers are written. The defaults are \exponentialE and \imaginaryI.

Behavior Changes​

  • A name in parentheses is a factor: (f)(x) is a product.
  • Lenient parsing accepts +- as ± and -+ as ∓.
  • Four diagnostic codes are renamed; update handlers that match them: letter-run-split → ambiguous-letter-run, implicit-product-in-denominator → ambiguous-denominator, spaced-digit-groups → ambiguous-digit-groups, and letter-before-decimal → ambiguous-letter-decimal.
  • LaTeX output uses standard notation for LCM, Log2, Log10, number sets and Degrees (#345, contributed by enumeratio).
  • A named call through a variable whose declared type gives no parameter names is the error argument-names-unavailable. For a variable declared with an unnamed signature, the error code was argument-name-unknown. Call such a variable with positional arguments, or declare it with a signature that names its parameters.
  • Lenient parsing reads mod, pow, trunc, Re and Im before a parenthesis as Mod, Power, Truncate, Real and Imaginary: mod(7, 3) evaluates to 1.

Issues Resolved​

  • Declared symbols mapped with vars remain run-time inputs even when they have assigned values. Integrals over mapped inputs retain closed forms. To force numeric quadrature with a mapping, use source other than a plain read, such as { a: '(_.a)' }.
  • Python and shader targets reject reserved identifier mappings and names.
  • Calls through record and dictionary fields respect declarations and named arguments. Caller symbols sharing parameter names retain their meaning (#390).
  • Custom libraries load in the requested dependency order, and standard-library selection includes required dependencies. Failed declarations restore the previous binding.
  • Derivatives and compilation respect unchanged copies of library definitions (#394). Minimal library configurations can construct function literals.
  • Numeric integration uses adaptive quadrature even when an integrand cannot compile. Imaginary factors serialize without unnecessary parentheses.
  • A prefix \mp or ∓ has a reading: \mp 1 is MinusPlus(0, 1). Calls whose arguments contain Floor, Ceil, Round or Truncate are no longer much slower than in 0.141.0.

0.144.0 2026-10-01​

New Features​

  • Lenient parsing accepts more plain-text notation: signed and compound exponents, full letter subscripts, in, infinity, sign, sgn, chained comparisons and √(x+1). Optional diagnostics flag ambiguous readings.
  • About reports examples and keywords, and lists operator attributes, including laziness (#398).

Behavior Changes​

  • Solve returns a free parameter for identities and remains symbolic when it has no justified candidate root (#397).
  • Exact rational Range bounds and steps produce exact elements (#397).
  • Logarithm combination and splitting require provably non-negative arguments (#397).
  • The attributes entry of About is a list of strings, not one string: About(Add) gives ["commutative", "associative", "idempotent", "lazy"]. A program that read the entry as a string must read it as a list.

Issues Resolved​

  • Solve handles more linear and logarithmic equations and preserves exact exponential roots: Solve(eˣ = 3, x) gives ln(3).
  • Derivatives respect custom library definitions and user replacements: after Sinh(x) := 3x, D(Sinh(t), t) is 3 (#393).
  • Library loading order and operator signature extensions behave consistently (#393, #394).
  • Corrected definition metadata and exact zero cases of LerchPhi (#397).
  • LaTeX avoids duplicate grouping, recognizes arccot, and reads scientific notation with a braced base 10. The resolveApplication hook sees names before parentheses consistently in lenient mode.

Performance​

  • Faster compiled JavaScript range processing and scalar callbacks (#387, #388). Deeply nested lenient exponents parse quickly.

0.143.0 2026-10-01​

New Features​

  • ReplaceAt, DeleteAt and Insert compile to JavaScript and Python (#386).
  • Max, Min, Length, Count, Sum and Product of an operand typed as an abstract collection compile to JavaScript (#385).

Behavior Changes​

  • Nested list types describe their corresponding matrix shapes.
  • Sum and Product preserve point, row and matrix result types.
  • Extrema of dictionaries and sums of nonnumeric scalar elements report type errors consistently.
  • A symbol declared with a nested list type is a matrix: with x declared list<list<integer^2>^2>, x^2 is the matrix power, not the square of each element.

Issues Resolved​

  • Compiled sums, products and reductions handle real and complex collections correctly, or decline unsupported shapes instead of returning NaN or strings.
  • Numeric Reduce over rows works without an initial value: Reduce([[1, 2], [3, 4]], Add).N() is [4, 6].
  • Compiled statistics no longer return incorrect values for nested lists, and annotated parameters validate absent arguments.
  • Arithmetic methods preserve assigned-variable dependencies; multiplication by zero no longer hides an assigned NaN.
  • Corrected function assignment for parameters that admit missing values, dictionary-join diagnostics and missing operands of Sum/Product.
  • HurwitzZeta supports integer orders with arguments far left of the imaginary axis. Simplification propagates NaN through extrema.

Performance​

  • Registering chains of dependent functions no longer takes exponential time.

0.142.0 2026-09-30​

New Features​

  • ce.conformsTo(type, protocol) queries protocol conformance (#362, contributed by enumeratio).
  • Collection length slots accept type variables. DMS angles accept additional arc-minute and arc-second spellings and can omit minutes (#364, proposed by enumeratio; #338, contributed by yelliver).

Behavior Changes​

  • Rounding, step functions and comparisons use exact operands under .N(). Two exact numbers compare without tolerance, including near boundaries.
  • Full materialization returns every element of a finite lazy collection (#380, reported by enumeratio).
  • Functions enforce explicitly annotated parameters, while unannotated parameters retain inferred behavior. Absent arguments at annotated parameters are errors; numeric parameters still accept NaN.
  • Assignments store the current elements of lazy collections that depend on variables. Known valid literal indices no longer add an absent result type.
  • Range, Linspace, comprehensions and Tabulate are typed list<T> (Tycho row 337).
  • A rounding function, Fract, Mod, Sign, Heaviside or a comparison of an exact constant expression is resolved under evaluate() by raising the precision: Floor(π·10³⁰) is the exact integer 3141592653589793238462643383279, and Fract(π) is π − 3.
  • To get the display preview from evaluate(), pass materialization: [5, 5]. toString() and .latex still print the preview.
  • To accept an absent argument at an annotated parameter, annotate it T | missing and test isMissing(p), or remove the absent case at the call (first(…) ?? fallback).
  • A function declared with ce.declare(name, { signature }) checks its evaluated arguments against the scalar parameter types. With f declared (integer) -> unknown and assigned x ↦ x + 1, f(1.5) gave 2.5 and is now an incompatible-type error.
  • A parenthesized derivative operand ends at its closing parenthesis: \frac{d}{dx}(x)+1 is D(x, x) + 1, where it was D(x + 1, x). A factor written after the parenthesis is outside the derivative: \frac{d}{dx}(x+1)(x-1) is D(x+1, x)·(x-1) (#336).

Issues Resolved​

  • Improved HurwitzZeta, Zeta, LerchPhi, PolyLog, incomplete gamma and high-order polygamma evaluation near poles, branch boundaries and difficult orders. More real arguments follow working precision; unreliable cases stay symbolic. More special functions broadcast over lists (#374, contributed by enumeratio).
  • Interval enclosures for Gamma, GammaLn, Binomial and Factorial contain their true values. Compiled binomial values agree outside 0 ≤ k ≤ n (#384, reported by enumeratio).
  • Lazy operators and compiled JavaScript handle collections that may be absent. Sums of points and rows retain their shape (#383).
  • Folds that build lists compile and preserve accumulator types. Recursive collection functions and destructuring loop declarations compile correctly (#369, reported by enumeratio; Tycho rows 338 and 339).
  • WGSL shaders using NaN or infinity compile in browsers. Shader LerchPhi and PolyLog support more arguments and improved accuracy.
  • Unsupported searches remain symbolic instead of reporting index 0. Invalid infinite indices and indeterminate integrands return consistent values (#368, reported by enumeratio).
  • Epsil serialization scales linearly with nesting depth. Nested function slots, complex literals, NaN patterns and absent set spreads behave consistently (#379, #381, reported by enumeratio).
  • Protocol dispatch binds Self to the selected implementation's type. Compiled ranges no longer capture user variables named i or _e (#362, contributed by enumeratio; #367, reported by enumeratio).
  • Floor, Ceil, Round, Truncate and Fract of an exact number are exact: Floor((25! − 1)/24!) was 25 and is now 24, and Fract((25! − 1)/3) was −1/3 and is now 2/3 (#382, reported by enumeratio).
  • A Pipe stage that uses no topic slot and whose value is not a function is an incompatible-type error: 5 |> Max(3) gave 3.
  • ce.number([n, 0]) is ~oo for n ≠ 0, as ce.box(["Rational", n, 0]) is; it was NaN. ce.number([0, 0]) is Indeterminate.
  • The materialization option no longer truncates the operands of an eager operator: Length(Range(1, 5000)).evaluate({ materialization: true }) was 11.
  • A fold's accumulator is typed from its seed and its combiner's result. Map and Filter over a fold that builds a list give a list: they gave a set (Set(7, 3, 5) where the fold's value is the list [6, 2, 4]).

Performance​

  • A predicate over a finite Range compiles to a counting loop on the JavaScript target, without building the range: Count, CountIf, Any, All, Length(Filter(…)) and Filter over a range (#373).
  • A protocol member call no longer parses the member's signature again at each call. A call on a scalar receiver costs about 1.3× an equivalent plain function, where it cost about 12× (#363, contributed by enumeratio).

0.141.0 2026-09-29​

New Features​

  • Added Indeterminate and isIndeterminate for exact indeterminate forms. 0/0 and other exact indeterminate calculations now use this value; .N() and compiled code use NaN. It is distinct from an absent value: IsMissing(Indeterminate) is False (#355).
  • epsil --compile compiles and runs JavaScript, using machine arithmetic. Unsupported constructs and unbound symbols report runtime errors.
  • ce.withStepBudget({ steps, label }, fn) bounds cooperative engine work. Exhaustion throws CancellationError with cause 'step-budget' (Tycho row 326).
  • Added LerchPhi(z, s, a), the Lerch transcendent, and support for non-integer and complex orders of PolyLog: PolyLog(2.5, 0.5).N() is about 0.5549972787175124. Unsupported numeric cases remain symbolic (#340, contributed by enumeratio).
  • PolyGamma, Digamma and Trigamma support complex arguments (#340, contributed by enumeratio).
  • Added exact eigenvalues for supported 2×2 and 3×3 matrices, plus evaluation of AdjugateMatrix and PseudoInverse.
  • PolyLog and LerchPhi compile to JavaScript, GLSL and WGSL for real operands.
  • CancellationCause gains 'step-budget', and isTimeoutCancellation is true for both a timeout and a spent step budget.

Behavior Changes​

  • Decimal spellings preserve floats through Epsil and LaTeX round trips, including integer-valued floats. Rounding a float produces an exact number (#351).
  • User functions that pass parameters to whole-collection operators receive lists whole. Operations on abstract collection types preserve possible broadcast result types.
  • Restricted infinite or unknown-length collections pair with list conditions over the conditions' length. List literals with spreads remain lists.
  • Indeterminate is a reserved name.
  • Code that tests a result with x.isSame(ce.NaN) no longer matches an exact indeterminate form: use x.isNaN, which is true for both values, or x.isIndeterminate. ["Divide", 0, 0] canonicalizes to Indeterminate.
  • A list literal with a spread canonicalizes to the new operator ListJoin: [...a, 0] is ListJoin(a, [0]), where it was Join(a, [0]).
  • An integer-valued float serializes as 2.0 in LaTeX and {num: "2.0"} in MathJSON, so it reads back as a float; it was 2. With fractionalDigits: 0 (LaTeX) or digits: {fractional: 0} (MathJSON) the integer spelling is kept.
  • -(2x) canonicalizes to Multiply(-2, x); it was Negate(Multiply(2, x)). -\frac{x}{2} is Multiply(-1/2, x), the same expression as -\frac{1}{2}x (#345, contributed by enumeratio).
  • Beta(2, 3), Zeta(3) and Lb(x) serialize to LaTeX as \mathrm{B}(2, 3), \zeta(3) and \log_2(x). A negative numeric fraction writes its sign in front: Rational(-1, 2) is -\frac{1}{2}, Divide(x, -4) is -\frac{x}{4}.
  • Map, Filter and Scan over a symbol declared collection<T> that holds a list give a list: Map(x ↦ 2x, P) for P = [3, 1, 1] is [6, 2, 2], where it was Set(6, 2).
  • ce.Zero.div(ce.PositiveInfinity) is 0, as the Divide operator gives; it was NaN. A float numerator over an infinity is the float 0.

Issues Resolved​

  • Closures preserve nested block locals and each loop iteration's variable. Recursion no longer overwrites caller indices or locals (Tycho row 330).
  • Unannotated Epsil helpers and collection-building recursion compile to JavaScript. Count(xs, predicate) also compiles (Tycho row 332).
  • vars mappings remain dynamic when reached through assigned expressions; program-defined functions are excluded from free symbols (Tycho row 328).
  • Definite integration handles absolute values and signs of linear arguments, integration by parts, and integration variables with assigned values (#352).
  • Improved hypergeometric accuracy and high precision real zeta evaluation. Complex Arcosh and incomplete gamma select correct values (#353, #354; #340, contributed by enumeratio).
  • Unknown-length indexing stays symbolic, collection restrictions retain their types, and list and set spreads use the supplied argument's elements (Tycho rows 331, 334 and 335).
  • Derivatives, negative large numbers, beta and zeta functions, logarithms and matrix rank serialize correctly. Epsil handles a * 2n and library names in the MCP compile tool (#345, contributed by enumeratio; Tycho row 333).
  • A compiled for loop over a list of complex values reads the loop variable as complex. It read it as real, so comparisons on it were false and divisions gave NaN (Tycho row 332).
  • More exact special values: Log(1/8, 2) and Lb(1/8) are -3, Sinc(Pi) is exactly 0, Arccot(1) is π/4, and ComplexRoots(1, 4) is [1, i, -1, -i].

Performance​

  • Type queries and declarations for nested dependent functions no longer take exponential time (Tycho rows 329 and 336).

0.140.0 2026-09-27​

New Features​

  • ce.number({ re, im }) accepts JavaScript numbers or BigDecimal values for each component.
  • isComplex is public on the number-literal interface.

Behavior Changes​

  • Decimal spellings consistently produce floats at machine precision, and a float operand makes numeric results inexact.
  • Integrate applies coordinate by coordinate to tuples.
  • More logical connectives use three-valued logic for absent operands. Compiled absent points, tuples and lists use undefined in arithmetic.
  • User bindings shadow capitalized library names. Binding Nothing, Missing or Undefined is an error.
  • Length of an infinite collection is +oo. StringFrom of text or a symbol returns its text.
  • serializeEpsil writes the lowercase spelling of a library name: ["Sin", "x"] is sin(x) and "Pi" is pi. The new option libraryNames: 'mathjson' restores the previous output, and the new isBound option reports names bound outside the expression.
  • A round trip through parseEpsil alone gives the raw lowercase head (["sin", "x"]). Run resolveLibraryNames to read it back to Sin.
  • isMachineNumeric is false for a number or list that holds an integer-valued float such as 2.0.
  • Timing returns an unnamed tuple, tuple<number, value>: read the parts as Timing(expr)[1] and Timing(expr)[2]. Timing(expr).result was an incompatible-type error.
  • x^{0.5} stays Power(x, 0.5). Only an exact 1/2 becomes \sqrt{x}.

Issues Resolved​

  • Complex results retain working precision and imaginary components outside double range. Exp(Ln(−2)).N() is −2.
